subject.title: [Feature]: Add tools.web.fetch.allowPrivateNetwork to allow private network access

question: Should OpenClaw expose broad private-network access for arbitrary `web_fetch` URLs, and if so should the public contract be global, per-agent, hostname-scoped, or folded into a broader egress policy?
rationale: The source shows the lower-level SSRF primitive exists, but exposing it changes a model-directed network boundary and a public config contract; automation should not choose the metadata/link-local, authorization, redirect, and cache semantics.

options.title: Approve Scoped SSRF Policy
options.body: Land a narrowly documented nested `tools.web.fetch.ssrfPolicy` design that enables private-network access only with explicit operator intent and complete security coverage.

options.title: Keep Current Strict Default Only
options.body: Leave arbitrary `web_fetch` private-network access unsupported for now and document the existing fake-IP/proxy-only exceptions.

options.title: Fold Into Egress Policy
options.body: Route this through the broader web-tool egress firewall work so private-network access, allowlists, and per-agent authorization are designed together.

recommendation.title: Approve Scoped SSRF Policy
recommendation.body: Land a narrowly documented nested `tools.web.fetch.ssrfPolicy` design that enables private-network access only with explicit operator intent and complete security coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest combined signal from the issue discussion and prior SSRF/web-fetch hardening history.
